issue.description:
Add the additive boolean auto_flush so a fleet detects the behaviour by handshake instead of inferring it from a version number.

The field reports the compiled default. A workspace that disables publication via checkpoint.auto_flush, and an invocation passing --no-auto-flush, do not change what the binary advertises; sync --status remains the only authority on whether a given workspace is clean.

Acceptance:
- auto_flush present once the default flips, absent before
- capability tests assert the advertised value matches actual binary behaviour
- documented as reporting the compiled default, not workspace state

Refs: plan section 11, 6.2.1; ADR-003.
issue.title: Advertise auto_flush in the capability document

issue.close_reason: Fixed in 9ed0123 (pushed to origin/main). Chose option 3 - treat expired/foreign lease rows as absent when the current claim was non-leased - implemented as claim-epoch scoping in validate_lease_for_mutation: when no ACTIVE lease matches the current assignee, the historical row only fences if it belongs to the current assignee AND the most recent 'claimed' event records a leased claim (with_lease:true; events.sequence is monotonic so no timestamp comparison). Rejected purge-on-release/close: leases.issue_id is the PRIMARY KEY, so the single row IS the per-issue fencing-token high-water mark (MAX(fencing_token)) - purging would reset tokens and break the monotonicity R002 documents. Verified live: the scripted repro (leased claim w1 -> release -> plain claim w2 -> close) now exits 0; expired lease of the CURRENT leased epoch still refuses with exit 4 (fencing unchanged); same-name plain re-claim also survives old-lease expiry. tests/r002_leased_claims.rs: new test_plain_reclaim_after_leased_release_is_mutable + all 10 originals pass; full cargo test 712 passed / 0 failed. Out-of-scope findings while investigating: (1) 'claim --fencing-token' on an issue that already has a lease row fails with 'UNIQUE constraint failed: leases.issue_id' (create_lease INSERTs rather than replacing - latent pre-existing bug); (2) an issue whose CURRENT leased epoch has expired remains unreleasable/unclosable with no operator override - pre-existing R002 stale-worker fencing semantics, unchanged here.
issue.description:
src/service/leases.rs:248-303 (validate_lease_for_mutation): when no ACTIVE lease matches (issue, current assignee), the mere existence of ANY historical lease row (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM leases WHERE issue_id = ?) raises Error::LeaseExpired. Lease rows are never deleted: release_issue_impl/close_issue_impl (src/service/lifecycle.rs:344-436) do not purge them and cleanup_expired_leases (leases.rs:342) is #[allow(dead_code)], never called. All four lifecycle ops call validate_lease_for_mutation whenever the issue has an assignee (lifecycle.rs:47,102,142,176).

Net effect: once an issue has EVER been claimed with --lease-ttl, any later NON-leased claimant is permanently locked out of close/release/update — the issue is stuck in_progress+assigned forever (the classic fleet-starvation shape) with no CLI recovery path (update --clear-assignee hits the same validation).

Reproduced live at HEAD (dac3910): 'bead claim --assignee w1 --lease-ttl 30' -> 'bead release <id>' -> 'bead claim --assignee w2' (plain) -> 'bead close <id> --reason done' fails exit 4 'Lease for issue ... has expired or is invalid for assignee w2'; release and update fail identically.

Fix options (pick one, document in the close reason): purge the issue's lease rows on release/close; or scope the 'lease existed' check to the current assignment epoch (e.g. leases created at/after the current claim event); or treat expired/foreign lease rows as absent when the current claim was non-leased.

Acceptance (run in repo):
1. Script the repro above in a temp workspace; w2's close now succeeds exit 0.
2. Active-holder fencing is unchanged: existing tests/r002_leased_claims.rs pass.
3. Regression test added to tests/r002_leased_claims.rs covering leased-claim -> release -> plain-claim -> close; cargo test passes.
issue.title: Stop lease history from permanently bricking mutation of re-claimed issues

issue.description:
Automatic flush introduces an outcome that does not exist today: the mutation succeeded and the checkpoint did not advance. Machine consumers must be able to tell that apart from the mutation not happening.

Acceptance:
- the mutation stays committed and visible
- the mutation's own success output is preserved on stdout
- the publication failure is reported on stderr
- the process exits 1, and exit 1 never implies rollback
- a test forces publication failure and asserts the mutation is still present

Refs: plan 6.2.1 item 5, section 5.2; ADR-003.
issue.title: Define split-failure semantics when a mutation commits and publication fails

issue.description:
Turn the explicit restore that plan section 7 already recommends into one verified command instead of an operator-reconstructed recipe. Select and verify a named immutable generation, refuse a non-empty target unless explicitly overridden, attribute the actor, and report exactly what was restored.

Restore stays explicit and never automatic — doctor continues to recommend and never perform it. This changes only whether the recommended path is executable, not the fail-closed rule.

Why now: the recovery path currently survives as lore, reconstructed from prose per incident by someone who has just discovered their store is broken. On 2026-08-14 an operator applied a foreign tool's recovery procedure to a native store, silently reinitializing it with the wrong schema; the data survived only because that workspace's checkpoint happened to be current. A named command is also the thing that can be pointed at when someone asks how to recover.

Acceptance:
- one command performs verify-source, empty-target guard, actor attribution, and reports what was restored
- refuses unverified artifacts and refuses R029 archaeology views as input, preserving their non-importability
- specification states plainly how this relates to sync import-only, including whether that path becomes internal
- doctor still never performs restore automatically
- provenance/receipt record written for the restore
- conformance scenarios for: empty target, non-empty target refused, override path, unverified source refused, R029 view refused

Refs: ADR-006; plan section 7 (fail-closed rule); plan section 12 R036; R029 (beadrs-2ba14020) non-importable views; R027 (beadrs-de075bba) healthy-store case; ADR-002.
issue.title: R036: First-class verified restore (bead restore)

issue.description:
Workspace discovery stops at the FIRST .beads directory on the upward walk and fails closed with a precise diagnostic when it lacks the bead-rs workspace fingerprint, instead of walking past a foreign store to an unrelated parent workspace. The diagnostic claims only that the directory is not a bead-rs workspace; identifying a foreign format stays prohibited. An explicit override permits legitimate nesting.

Motivated by the 2026-08-14 SEAM wrong-CLI-against-wrong-store incident class.

Acceptance:
- discovery terminates at any .beads directory encountered
- non-bead-rs .beads yields a fail-closed diagnostic naming the path, not the foreign format
- explicit override flag documented and tested for legitimate nesting
- section 4.1 discovery prose updated with the new rule

Refs: plan section 12 R030; ideas-ledger 2026-08-15 finalist 3 dossier.
issue.notes:
FIELD EVIDENCE 2026-08-16 — argues for scheduling this early, as R030's own text allows.

On 2026-08-14 a workspace was structurally damaged because the operator could not
tell which tool owned a store: a foreign recovery procedure was applied to a
native store and silently reinitialized it with the wrong schema. The data
survived only because that workspace's checkpoint happened to be current.

The fail-closed diagnostic this bead specifies is the intervention that stops
that class of loss, and it remains sayable within the clean-room boundary — the
message claims only that the directory is not a bead-rs workspace, never that it
is some identified foreign format.

Downstream environment documentation currently carries this as an operator rule
("always check which backend a repo uses before running a bead command"), which
is exactly the kind of load-bearing lore this bead retires.

Plan section 12 R030 updated with this evidence in b634991.
issue.title: R030: Self-defending workspace discovery (stop at first .beads, fail closed)

issue.description:

A claim atomically acquires every key its bead declares and excludes ready issues needing a key currently held; release, close, and lease expiry return keys. Acceptance:
- resource-key validation, acquisition/release lifecycle, and migration specified

Refs: plan section 12 R031; ideas-ledger 2026-08-15 finalist 4 dossier; run-1 finalist 5.

issue.description:
One verified read-only loader materializes a named checkpoint artifact (pointer, manifest, or monolith) into an ephemeral view serving: query against a historical generation without import; a semantic issue/event-level diff between two generations; and predicate-driven search across a generation series. Views are never accepted as import input; outputs are explicitly non-importable.

Acceptance:
- query --checkpoint PATH answers list/query against a committed generation read-only
- sync diff A B reports issue/event-level semantic delta between two generations
- archaeology outputs rejected by every import path
- loader reuses existing verification (hashes, counts, ordering) before serving any view

Refs: plan section 12 R029; ideas-ledger 2026-08-15 finalist 8 dossier (archaeology).
issue.title: R029: Checkpoint archaeology (query/diff/bisect over committed generations)

issue.description:
Automatic flush makes concurrent workers contend on checkpoint publication, not just on SQLite. Publication needs its own serialization so a lost race degrades to success rather than to a torn pointer.

Acceptance:
- publication is serialized by a checkpoint lock separate from the SQLite write path
- a worker finding a newer generation already published for a sequence at or beyond its own treats it as success and exits 0
- bounded concurrent workers produce no torn pointer and no partially applied tombstone set
- at quiesce every worker's committed sequence is covered by some published generation

Refs: plan 6.2.1 item 4; ADR-003.
issue.title: Serialize checkpoint publication with a lock distinct from the SQLite write path

issue.description:
src/service/leases.rs:167-178: renew_lease executes 'UPDATE leases SET assignee = ?1, fencing_token = ?2, expires_at = ?3, renewed_at = ?4 WHERE issue_id = ?5' — no assignee predicate. Because create_lease (leases.rs:89-100) INSERTs a fresh row for every leased claim and nothing ever deletes rows, an issue accumulates multiple lease rows over its life; one renewal then rewrites EVERY row for the issue, stamping them all with the renewer's assignee/token/expiry and destroying the per-row lease history the fencing model (monotonic tokens, R002) relies on for auditability.

Fix: constrain the UPDATE with 'AND assignee = ?' (and preferably target only the active row, e.g. the row with MAX(fencing_token) or expires_at > now), and decide/document whether repeated claims should keep inserting new rows or reuse one row per issue.

Acceptance (run in repo):
1. Integration/unit test that produces two lease rows for one issue (leased claim -> release -> leased claim by another assignee, using the post-beadrs-122d91fb behavior), renews one lease, and asserts the other row's assignee/fencing_token/expires_at are unchanged.
2. Existing tests/r002_leased_claims.rs passes.
3. cargo test passes.

Note: blocked by beadrs-122d91fb because both change src/service/leases.rs and the chosen fix there (e.g. purging rows on release/close) changes what this bead must assert.
issue.title: Scope renew_lease UPDATE to the renewing assignee's lease row

issue.description:
Automatic flush must be a no-op when the covered sequence already equals the live event sequence, so a no-op mutation publishes no generation and creates no object.

This rule is only sound once every semantic mutation advances the sequence, which is why it depends on the event work.

Acceptance:
- a mutation that changes nothing publishes no new generation
- a real mutation publishes exactly one generation covering its own sequence
- sync flush-only against a clean checkpoint publishes nothing and exits 0

Refs: plan 6.2.1 items 3 and 8; ADR-003.
issue.title: Skip automatic publication when the checkpoint already covers the live sequence

issue.close_reason: Fixed in 3f720bb (pushed to origin main). The double-claim path itself had already been removed by 6662c31; this change completes the fix by building the --why trace from a pre-claim eligibility snapshot (collect_eligibility_factors + build_decision_trace) so selected_factors and the eligibility summary describe decision-time state instead of contradicting the selection. Regression test added; all acceptance criteria verified live on FIFO and policy paths; full cargo test green.
issue.description:
src/main.rs:157-163: cmd_claim calls service::claim_issue_with_trace AFTER the real claim (main.rs:121-154) inside the same committed transaction, and claim_issue_with_trace (src/service/claim.rs:673-696) performs a full claim_issue mutation. So 'bead claim --why' claims TWO beads and silently discards the second ID.

Reproduced live at HEAD (dac3910): fresh workspace, 3 ready beads, one 'bead claim --assignee w1 --why' left TWO beads in_progress assigned to w1. Also the JSON output is self-contradictory: decision_trace.selected_issue_id names the second (hidden) bead while claim_result.bead_id names the first, and selected_factors reports the bead as in_progress/ineligible because the trace is computed after the mutation.

Fix: never invoke the mutating claim path a second time; compute the trace with the read-only create_decision_trace (claim.rs:577) against the bead the first claim actually selected, before/without mutating again. Applies to both FIFO and --policy paths.

Acceptance (run in repo):
1. Fresh temp workspace, >=2 ready beads; 'bead claim --assignee w1 --why' then 'bead list --status in_progress --json' shows exactly ONE issue.
2. In 'bead claim --assignee w1 --why --json', decision_trace.selected_issue_id == claim_result.bead_id.
3. Regression test added (tests/r001_decision_traces.rs or tests/cli_claim.rs) asserting single-claim under --why; cargo test passes.
issue.notes: Found at dispatch time that the hidden second claim was already gone at HEAD: 6662c31 (beadrs-b412cc80, landed 2026-08-20) replaced cmd_claim's claim_issue_with_trace call with the read-only create_decision_trace, so criteria 1 (exactly one in_progress) and 2 (selected_issue_id == claim_result.bead_id) already passed. What remained was the other half of the reproduced bug: the trace was assembled from post-mutation state, so selected_factors reported the just-claimed bead as in_progress/assigned/ineligible and the eligibility summary counted it under already_assigned/not_open_status. Fixed in 3f720bb: split create_decision_trace into public read-only collect_eligibility_factors + new build_decision_trace(factors, selected, assignee); cmd_claim (FIFO and --policy paths) now snapshots factors before the claim and assembles the trace afterwards against the bead actually selected; claim_issue_with_trace snapshots the same way. Regression test test_claim_with_why_claims_exactly_one_issue added in tests/r001_decision_traces.rs. Verified live on both paths (fifo-v1 and aging-v1): one in_progress, IDs match, selected_factors shows open/unassigned/eligible. cargo fmt clean, clippy clean, full cargo test 38/38 binaries ok.
issue.title: Fix 'bead claim --why' performing a second hidden claim in cmd_claim

issue.description:
Every mutating command in main.rs independently discovers the workspace, opens its own rusqlite connection, commits, and prints. There is no shared path a publication step could hook.

Introduce one shared post-commit chokepoint so every present and future mutating command inherits identical publication behavior, rather than editing ~20 call sites. Publication runs after the transaction commits, never inside it, so a publication failure cannot roll back committed work. Read-only commands never publish.

Acceptance:
- one chokepoint, exercised by all mutating commands
- publication is strictly after commit
- read-only commands do not publish
- adding a mutating command inherits publication without touching its call site

Refs: plan 6.2.1 items 1-2; ADR-003.
issue.title: Add a single post-commit checkpoint publication chokepoint

issue.description:
Where a command rejects an argument a competent operator would expect to work, state the domain rule and the remedy instead of surfacing a bare parser error. Generalizes the standard `release` already sets when it refuses an assigned open issue with "use 'update --clear-assignee' instead".

Verified against the shipped CLI 2026-08-16:

  bead update <id> --title "x"  -> error: unexpected argument '--title' found
                                   tip: to pass '--title' as a value, use '-- --title'
  bead close <id> --body "x"    -> error: unexpected argument '--body' found
                                   tip: to pass '--body' as a value, use '-- --body'

Both are actively misleading: the tip proposes escaping the flag as a positional value, which is never the intent and produces a second confusing failure if followed. Neither states the actual rule. Both are load-bearing enough that downstream environment documentation carries explicit warnings about them.

No currently-rejected invocation becomes accepted. No semantics change. This is message quality only.

Acceptance:
- fields immutable after create (title, description, priority, issue-type) produce an error naming the rule and any supported alternative, e.g. label add|remove for labels
- close --body names --reason
- near-miss handling is bounded to flags that exist on sibling commands, not general fuzzy matching
- conformance scenarios assert the remedy text, not merely a nonzero exit, so the affordance cannot regress to a parser default

Refs: ADR-007; plan section 5 command and process contract; plan section 12 R037.
issue.title: R037: Command errors that name the remedy

issue.close_reason: ref add and ref remove now append one audit event in their own transaction (external_ref_added / external_ref_removed) with namespace and key in the detail. Values are never recorded verbatim — only a SHA-256 fingerprint — since R011 values are free-form and can carry a credential-shaped string. Events are gated on semantic change: an identical re-add (upsert no-op) and a remove that deletes nothing append nothing; a changed-value re-add does append. Unit + CLI tests cover event shape, redaction, no-ops, and per-mutation advance of `bead changes --latest`; full cargo test green (685 passed). Shipped in faae4b7.

- bead changes --latest advances per mutation

Refs: plan 6.2.1 P3; ADR-003.

issue.description:
src/service/lifecycle.rs: update_issue (14-77), release_issue (80-111), close_issue (114-151), reopen_issue (154-185) all read the issue via get_issue_for_update and validate the --if-revision guard BEFORE starting the write transaction (conn.unchecked_transaction() at lines 65, 106, 146, 180), and the subsequent UPDATE statements match on 'WHERE id = ?' only, with no revision predicate (lines 319, 354, 416, 450 — each does revision = revision + 1 unconditionally).

TOCTOU: a concurrent process (multi-worker shared workspace is the supported model) can commit a change between the pre-transaction read and the write; the guard then passes against the stale revision and the update silently overwrites newer state — exactly the lost update README lines 128-130 promises fails with exit 4. The window is real for separate-process SQLite WAL connections; unchecked_transaction is deferred, so no write lock is held during validation.

Fix: perform the read + revision/lease validation INSIDE the transaction (and take it immediate so the snapshot cannot go stale before the write), or make each UPDATE conditional ('WHERE id = ? AND revision = ?') and map 0 affected rows to the existing conflict/exit-4 path.

Acceptance (run in repo):
1. New test with two connections to one workspace: conn A reads revision N; conn B performs an update (revision becomes N+1); conn A then runs a lifecycle op with --if-revision N and MUST get the conflict error (exit 4 semantics), not success.
2. Existing tests/r003_revision_guards.rs passes unchanged.
3. cargo test passes.
issue.title: Enforce --if-revision atomically inside the lifecycle write transaction

issue.description:
create --unique-ref NAMESPACE:KEY binds an R011 external reference inside the insert transaction; when the reference is already bound, the command returns the existing bead's identity instead of creating a duplicate. The closed-bead case must be explicit (distinct output or flagged conflict) so automation cannot loop on finished work.

Prevents duplicate beads at the source when dispatchers materialize work from the same external identifier concurrently.

Acceptance:
- ref binding and duplicate detection occur in one insert transaction
- ref-hit returns the existing ID with output distinguishable from a fresh create
- closed-bead ref-hit semantics explicit and tested
- concurrent duplicate-create race test: exactly one bead exists afterwards

Refs: plan section 12 R032; ideas-ledger 2026-08-15 finalist 5 dossier.
issue.notes:
ADR-008 (2026-08-16) records that title-similarity duplicate detection was
considered and REJECTED, and routes duplicate prevention here.

Rationale: ADR-001 already settled that this project does not infer from issue
titles "under any circumstance", and a soft warning is not a weaker commitment —
it still needs a similarity function and threshold, and still fires on sibling
beads, which are normal in this domain. R032's transactional unique-ref is the
only mechanism that can actually guarantee non-duplication.

Consequence for this bead: R032 is now the sole sanctioned answer to "how do I
stop duplicate beads", so its closed-bead case matters more than the plan text
implies. Anyone asking for fuzzy duplicate detection should be directed here.
issue.title: R032: Idempotent create by unique reference (create --unique-ref)

issue.description:
src/store/sqlite.rs:58-75 and src/store/mod.rs:116-131 deliberately configure every store connection with PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON, busy_timeout=5000, journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL. But ~25 command handlers in src/main.rs open raw rusqlite::Connection::open(&db_path) with NONE of these (lines 109, 271, 308, 379, 443, 488, 517, 552, 600, 622, 651, 726, 777, 808, 833, 873, 918, 1034, 1468, 1619, 2110, 2263, 2356), as do src/service/doctor.rs:451 and 495.

Consequences: (a) SQLite foreign_keys defaults OFF per-connection, so every 'FOREIGN KEY ... ON DELETE CASCADE' declared in src/store/migrations.rs (lines 128-412) is unenforced on the CLI's primary code paths; (b) busy_timeout=0 means concurrent fleet access (multiple workers running bead claim/update against one workspace, the tool's core use case) hits immediate SQLITE_BUSY -> exit 1 instead of waiting up to 5s, undermining the concurrent-claim contract documented in README 'Coordinating a fleet'. cmd_claim (main.rs:102-116) also uses unchecked_transaction (deferred) on such a raw connection.

Fix: add one shared helper (e.g. in src/store) that opens + applies the same pragmas as SqliteStore, and use it from every handler in main.rs and doctor.rs; remove direct Connection::open calls there.

Acceptance (run in repo):
1. grep -n "Connection::open(" src/main.rs src/service/doctor.rs returns no raw call sites (only the shared helper, or nothing).
2. A test asserts the connection used by a representative handler has foreign_keys=1 and busy_timeout=5000 (query 'PRAGMA foreign_keys; PRAGMA busy_timeout;').
3. cargo test passes.
issue.title: Route all main.rs command handlers through a shared pragma-configured connection opener

issue.description:
## Problem

bead claim has no check for whether the requesting assignee already holds an in_progress issue elsewhere in the same workspace. This lets one assignee accumulate unbounded simultaneous in_progress claims with no upper limit.

Real incident (2026-08-17, commitgraph workspace, a NEEDLE-fleet consumer of bead-rs): one assignee (claude-code-glm-5-commitgraph-2) held 9 simultaneous in_progress beads, another (claude-code-glm-5-adr018) held 8. All 25 in_progress beads in that workspace were confirmed stale (no live process working the repo; last real file touch predated even the freshest claim's updated_at) and released by hand. Ready frontier went 0 -> 22 after release.

## Proposed behavior

Add an opt-in claim-time guard, following the same per-call opt-in pattern leasing already uses (src/service/leases.rs: DEFAULT_LEASE_TTL/MIN_LEASE_TTL/MAX_LEASE_TTL are caller-supplied via the existing --lease-ttl flag on bead claim, not stored workspace config -- this should work the same way, not as a .beads/config.json default).

Proposed flag: bead claim --assignee X --single-claim (name TBD). When set, claim_issue (src/service/claim.rs:130) checks -- within the same transaction, same workspace database, before find_eligible_issue (claim.rs:638) / find_eligible_frontier (claim.rs:829) run -- whether X already has any issue with base status in_progress in this workspace. If so, refuse with a new ReasonCode (e.g. AssigneeHasActiveClaim) naming the blocking issue ID, rather than proceeding to select and assign a new one.

Scoped to this workspace's own database only. bead-rs stores are already one-per-workspace (one beads.db per repo), so this is a same-transaction query against the local issues table -- no cross-workspace lookup is needed or possible, and none is wanted: the point is per-workspace containment, not a global assignee registry.

## What this does and doesn't fix

Bounds impact, does not eliminate staleness. An assignee can still abandon their one claim and let it go stale -- this guard doesn't detect or reap that, it only prevents accumulation. With it, the ceiling is 1 stale claim per assignee per workspace, not unbounded.

Complementary to, not a replacement for:
- needle-d9a36be9 (NEEDLE): mend's own-newer-claim detection heuristic -- backstop for whatever still goes stale within the ceiling of 1
- Adopting the existing --lease-ttl mechanism in NEEDLE's claim path -- bounds how long that 1 stale claim can persist before another worker can reclaim it

## Scope: only the claim action itself

Applies only to the path where claim_issue / claim_issue_with_lease / claim_issue_with_policy newly assigns a previously-unassigned ready issue to an assignee -- i.e. where the assignee relationship is first established by a claim. Does NOT apply to other paths that set an assignee on an issue, e.g. bead update --assignee on an already-open issue. That is a distinct, already-tracked bug shape (NEEDLE bead needle-44e7e5cd: open+assignee issues invisible to the ready frontier, not a real active claim) with different consequences and should not be entangled with this guard.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] New opt-in flag on bead claim (e.g. --single-claim); default behavior unchanged when the flag is omitted
- [ ] With the flag set, claim fails with a distinct, machine-readable reason (new ReasonCode) when the assignee already holds an in_progress issue in this workspace, naming the blocking issue ID
- [ ] The check runs inside the same atomic transaction as selection/assignment -- no race between check and assign
- [ ] Does not alter bead update --assignee behavior on open issues
- [ ] Fixture: assignee holds one in_progress issue; bead claim --single-claim for the same assignee returns AssigneeHasActiveClaim and assigns nothing; after releasing or closing that issue, the same assignee can claim normally again
issue.title: bead claim: refuse a new claim when the assignee already holds an in_progress issue in this workspace

issue.description:
Report open beads that carry an assignee. Such a bead is not an active claim — a claim sets in_progress — but it IS excluded from the ready frontier, so no worker will ever select it. Advisory only: doctor never clears an assignee, because a parked reservation and abandoned residue are indistinguishable at the schema level and only the operator knows which is which. R034's sibling for the open lifecycle state.

The initial check shipped in 18fa7ee ahead of reason-code convergence and currently emits prose. This bead covers closing that gap, not the initial implementation.

Field evidence 2026-08-16: 583 beads in this state across 47 of 66 workspaces, ten with an entirely empty ready frontier while workers starved and every diagnostic reported clean. Median age 26h, oldest 37h. In one workspace 39 of 40 had zero active blockers — assignment alone held them.

Acceptance:
- emits stable R001-namespace reason codes rather than prose, matching R034's requirement to share semantics rather than invent parallel ones
- machine-readable list of held ids, not ids embedded in a message string
- decide and specify whether an intentionally-held assignment can be declared, so the warning stays meaningful in workspaces that park work on purpose
- doctor still never clears an assignee, including under --repair
- conformance scenario covering healthy -> warning -> cleared

issue.notes:
ADR-009 (2026-08-16) records that making bead-rs Git-aware — detecting unpulled
upstream changes to .beads/ before a flush — was considered and REJECTED, and
routes the underlying hazard here.

Rationale: R027 already states "bead-rs still never runs Git". Detecting the
store STATE (a verified checkpoint ahead of live) is strictly better than
detecting one transport: it is accurate regardless of how the checkpoint
arrived, and avoids importing Git's failure modes (detached heads, absent or
multiple remotes, shallow clones, worktrees, auth failures on a network probe)
into the flush path, where a false verdict from a safety check is worst.

Consequence for this bead: until R027 ships, the "pull before flush" ordering
rule remains unenforced operator discipline in Git-transported deployments, and
downstream documentation carries it as a standing rule. ADR-009 also asks that
R027's specification describe the Git-transported workflow it reconciles, so the
hazard is documented in-project rather than only downstream.
issue.title: R027: Remote-advanced checkpoint reconcile (bead sync reconcile)

## Genesis Bead

Authorized by: docs/adr/003-automatic-checkpoint-flush-gated-on-incremental-publication.md

## Overview
Make a successful semantic mutation publish a checkpoint generation covering its own committed sequence, replacing explicit sync flush-only as the default, so the durable checkpoint is never silently behind the database.

Gated. Per-mutation publication against the current path would write bytes quadratic in mutation count into a Git-tracked directory: flush is linear in workspace size, each generation leaks a full-workspace-sized object that is never collected, and most mutation kinds never advance the sequence that signals a flush is needed. The prerequisites are the implementation converging on plan sections 6.1.1 and 6.2 as already written; each is worth fixing whether or not the default ever changes.

bead-rs still never invokes Git. Automatic Git publication remains rejected.

## Progress
- [ ] P1: content-addressed monolithic root
- [ ] P2: applied pointer-declared tombstones
- [ ] P3: audit event for every committed semantic mutation (create, dep, ref, data, enumeration test)
- [ ] P4: reachable sharded publication
- [ ] A1-A6: chokepoint, skip-when-clean, publication lock, split-failure semantics, escape hatches, capability handshake
- [ ] A7: documentation reversal
- [ ] A8: activation gate evidence, then flip the default

detail.reason: Monolithic root is now objects/<sha256>.jsonl, named from its content SHA-256 like the sharded writer (checkpoint.rs publish_monolithic_checkpoint); identical content resolves to one object and a repeat publication keeps the existing file. Read paths resolve active_root.path from the pointer, so existing generation-named objects remain readable with no migration. Tests: name/hash agreement + not-generation-named (test_f017_content_addressed_paths), two identical flushes -> exactly 1 object with distinct generation ids (test_f017_identical_flushes_reuse_one_object), legacy objects/gen-*.jsonl layout imports via sync import-only --restore-into-empty (test_f017_legacy_generation_named_object_importable). Full suite 649 passed/1 failed -- the failure is test_capabilities_native_profile caused by a separate in-flight uncommitted edit to src/service/capabilities.rs (passes with that file stashed; unrelated to this change). fmt clean on touched files, clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean. Shipped as 95b59ad, pushed to origin/main.

Shipped in be427cd: tombstones applied after pointer commit, current.json never self-declared, retained set bounded to the two referenced generations, sync status gates on unresolved tombstones, cleanup crash-safe and repeatable. Suite 653/0, verified against this workspace's live 22-object backlog.

create_issue now appends a created audit event via a shared append_created_event helper on the caller's connection, inside the caller's transaction (same shape as the recurrence path, actor=system). Verified: 2 creates -> events sequences 1,2, changes --latest 0->1->2 with exactly one created mutation per create; mid-transaction failure (duplicate label PK after both rows inserted) rolls the event back with the issue (issues=2, events=2, cursor unchanged). New tests in cli_create.rs and r013_change_feed.rs; cli_sync.rs flush fixtures and a stale clone_recovery.rs comment updated for the event records now present in forensic.jsonl. Full suite green (fmt, clippy, 38 test binaries). Shipped in a10a1a5.

dep add and dep remove now each append one audit event (dependency_added / dependency_removed) inside their own transaction via a shared append_dependency_event helper; detail records blocked, blocker, and kind (plus condition for conditional adds). Events are gated on rows actually changed, so idempotent no-op re-adds and re-removes append nothing. Covered by unit tests and a bead changes --latest CLI test; full suite (38 binaries) plus fmt and clippy clean. Shipped in 52160d4.

ref add and ref remove now append one audit event in their own transaction (external_ref_added / external_ref_removed) with namespace and key in the detail. Values are never recorded verbatim — only a SHA-256 fingerprint — since R011 values are free-form and can carry a credential-shaped string. Events are gated on semantic change: an identical re-add (upsert no-op) and a remove that deletes nothing append nothing; a changed-value re-add does append. Unit + CLI tests cover event shape, redaction, no-ops, and per-mutation advance of `bead changes --latest`; full cargo test green (685 passed). Shipped in faae4b7.

set_data and remove_data now append data_set/data_removed audit events inside their own transactions via a shared append_data_event helper. Detail records namespace and schema_ref only (the removed row's schema_ref is captured pre-delete); the document body never enters the event log. Events are gated on semantic change: identical re-set and no-op remove append nothing, so bead changes --latest advances exactly once per real mutation. Fixed in 0b5d502; unit + CLI tests cover shape, redaction, no-ops, and per-mutation cursor advance; full suite green.

Implemented opt-in --single-claim guard: claim refuses with reason code assignee_has_active_claim (exit 4) naming the blocking issue when the assignee already holds in_progress work in the workspace; check runs in the same transaction as selection/assignment; lease renewal and update --assignee unaffected; default behavior unchanged. Includes fixture tests (refusal, release/close reclaim, multi-claim default, update-assignee scope, lease renewal) and a fix for the --why double-claim trace path. Shipped in 6662c31.

Fixed in 3f720bb (pushed to origin main). The double-claim path itself had already been removed by 6662c31; this change completes the fix by building the --why trace from a pre-claim eligibility snapshot (collect_eligibility_factors + build_decision_trace) so selected_factors and the eligibility summary describe decision-time state instead of contradicting the selection. Regression test added; all acceptance criteria verified live on FIFO and policy paths; full cargo test green.

Fixed in 9ed0123 (pushed to origin/main). Chose option 3 - treat expired/foreign lease rows as absent when the current claim was non-leased - implemented as claim-epoch scoping in validate_lease_for_mutation: when no ACTIVE lease matches the current assignee, the historical row only fences if it belongs to the current assignee AND the most recent 'claimed' event records a leased claim (with_lease:true; events.sequence is monotonic so no timestamp comparison). Rejected purge-on-release/close: leases.issue_id is the PRIMARY KEY, so the single row IS the per-issue fencing-token high-water mark (MAX(fencing_token)) - purging would reset tokens and break the monotonicity R002 documents. Verified live: the scripted repro (leased claim w1 -> release -> plain claim w2 -> close) now exits 0; expired lease of the CURRENT leased epoch still refuses with exit 4 (fencing unchanged); same-name plain re-claim also survives old-lease expiry. tests/r002_leased_claims.rs: new test_plain_reclaim_after_leased_release_is_mutable + all 10 originals pass; full cargo test 712 passed / 0 failed. Out-of-scope findings while investigating: (1) 'claim --fencing-token' on an issue that already has a lease row fails with 'UNIQUE constraint failed: leases.issue_id' (create_lease INSERTs rather than replacing - latent pre-existing bug); (2) an issue whose CURRENT leased epoch has expired remains unreleasable/unclosable with no operator override - pre-existing R002 stale-worker fencing semantics, unchanged here.

Shipped in f353b85. New contract suite tests/mutating_command_event_contract.rs walks the live clap tree and requires every visible leaf command to carry an explicit Mutating/NonMutating classification: mutating commands are invoked once against a fixture workspace and must advance the live event sequence, non-mutating ones must not advance it and must not alter the visible issue set. The plan section 5 command table is cross-checked against the registry, so plan drift and unclassified new commands both fail the suite; a mutating command without its event fails it too (verified by reverting the label fix and watching the suite catch label add). Label add/remove were the last unrecorded mutating paths and now append label_added/label_removed in the mutation's own transaction, skipping only idempotent no-ops. Full suite 724 passed / 0 failed; fmt and clippy clean.
